title: AI EARNINGS SPLIT: APPLOVIN +56%, DATADOG -25% AFTER A BEAT, BROADCOM'S $520 TARGET
author: tickeron_community
selftext:
AI and software names split hard after earnings. Some 30-day winners  
are still riding a beat, some beat and still sold off, and a few big  
average targets are still hanging out there. The 30-day figures below  
are from today's write-ups, not live quotes.  
  
Here is the scorecard from today's write-ups.  
  
\*\*1. Broadcom (AVGO)\*\* — The $520 central target is the average of  
roughly 30 verified analyst targets, rounded from about $519. With  
AVGO near $333.40, reaching $520 would take a gain of about 56%.  
Target, not a promise.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/broadcom-avgo-could-climb-56-to-meet-520-analyst-target-39307/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/broadcom-avgo-could-climb-56-to-meet-520-analyst-target-39307/)  
  
\*\*2. AppLovin (APP)\*\* — Shares climbed about 56% over 30 days, from  
about $262 in mid-October to $409.10 at the November 13 close — not a  
live quote. The move followed a Q3 beat: revenue rose 55% to $2.185  
billion, with diluted EPS of $4.30, both above consensus.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/applovin-app-climbs-56-in-30-days-on-earnings-strength-and-ai-progress-38455/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/applovin-app-climbs-56-in-30-days-on-earnings-strength-and-ai-progress-38455/)  
  
\*\*3. Datadog (DDOG)\*\* — Shares fell about 25% over 30 days, from about  
$247 to about $184 as of the latest close in the write-up, not a live  
quote. Q3 beat estimates, but Q4 guidance signaled a sharp growth  
slowdown.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/datadog-ddog-drops-25-in-30-days-earnings-beat-but-guidance-disappoints-38458/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/datadog-ddog-drops-25-in-30-days-earnings-beat-but-guidance-disappoints-38458/)  
  
\*\*4. Meta Platforms (META)\*\* — Shares fell about 11.7% over 30 days,  
from about $709.33 to $626.61, giving back a large chunk of a  
September rally. Those prices are from the write-up, not live quotes.  
Q3 revenue still rose 26% to $64.6 billion, above consensus, led by a  
26% gain in advertising.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/meta-platforms-meta-falls-11-7-in-30-days-despite-strong-q3-results-39308/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/meta-platforms-meta-falls-11-7-in-30-days-despite-strong-q3-results-39308/)  
  
\*\*5. MKS Instruments (MKSI)\*\* — The $290 central target is the average  
of six recently revised analyst targets, rounded from about $289. From  
about $215.65, that implies about 34% upside. Target, not a promise.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/mks-instruments-mksi-34-upside-to-the-290-analyst-target-38473/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/mks-instruments-mksi-34-upside-to-the-290-analyst-target-38473/)  
  
\*\*6. Spotify (SPOT)\*\* — Shares rose about 16.9% over 30 days, from  
about $524 to around $613, per the write-up's mid-November figures,  
not a live quote. The move was anchored by Q3 results on October 22,  
with record gross margin and faster advertising growth.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/spotify-spot-advances-16-9-in-30-days-on-strong-q3-results-38514/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/spotify-spot-advances-16-9-in-30-days-on-strong-q3-results-38514/)  
  
\*\*7. Equinix (EQIX)\*\* — The $1,230 central target is the average of 25  
verified analyst targets, rounded from about $1,232. From a recent  
close of $1,053.79, that implies about 17% upside. Target, not a  
promise.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/equinix-eqix-can-it-reach-17-upside-to-the-1-230-target-38470/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/equinix-eqix-can-it-reach-17-upside-to-the-1-230-target-38470/)  
  
\*\*8. POET Technologies (POET)\*\* — The $8.00 target is a single-analyst  
objective, not a broad consensus — coverage is very thin. From about  
$5.13, reaching $8.00 would take a gain of about 56%. Target, not a  
promise.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/poet-technologies-poet-assessing-the-path-to-the-8-00-target-and-56-upside-potential-39348/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/poet-technologies-poet-assessing-the-path-to-the-8-00-target-and-56-upside-potential-39348/)  
  
\*\*9. Duos Technologies (DUOT)\*\* — Q3 revenue of $10.5 million more  
than doubled year over year, but it missed a consensus range of about  
$12.8 million to $14.8 million. The GAAP diluted loss of $0.22 from  
continuing operations was wider than the Street expected.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/duos-technologies-duot-q3-results-show-102-revenue-growth-amid-ongoing-transformation-39389/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/duos-technologies-duot-q3-results-show-102-revenue-growth-amid-ongoing-transformation-39389/)  
  
\*\*10. Fiserv (FISV)\*\* — Shares rose about 34% over 30 days, from about  
$47.55 in mid-October to $63.78 by mid-November, per the write-up, not  
a live quote. The rally followed Q3, when Fiserv doubled its Project  
Elevate cost-savings target to $1 billion and announced a $500 million  
Q4 buyback.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/fiserv-fisv-shares-climb-34-over-30-days-on-earnings-momentum-38457/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/fiserv-fisv-shares-climb-34-over-30-days-on-earnings-momentum-38457/)  
  
\*\*11. Cycurion (CYCU)\*\* — Q3 revenue rose 40% to $5.38 million, above  
the company-cited consensus of $4.37 million. Gross margin jumped to  
36% from 7% a year earlier. These are small-cap numbers, so size them  
accordingly.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/cycurion-cycu-delivers-40-revenue-growth-in-q3-2026-as-gross-margins-expand-sharply-39409/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/cycurion-cycu-delivers-40-revenue-growth-in-q3-2026-as-gross-margins-expand-sharply-39409/)  
  
\*\*12. Research Solutions (RSSS)\*\* — Total revenue of $11.9 million  
fell 3.3% year over year. B2B ARR grew 11.5% to $16.5 million, and  
AI-related ARR rose 38% sequentially to $1.1 million.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/research-solutions-rsss-delivers-flat-earnings-as-b2b-and-ai-arr-gain-momentum-39410/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/research-solutions-rsss-delivers-flat-earnings-as-b2b-and-ai-arr-gain-momentum-39410/)  
  
\*\*13. QLYS vs TENB\*\* — Two cybersecurity names, one post-earnings  
head-to-head. Who comes out ahead? The breakdown is in the link.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/qualys-qlys-vs-tenable-tenb-weighing-momentum-in-cybersecurity-after-earnings-39282/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/qualys-qlys-vs-tenable-tenb-weighing-momentum-in-cybersecurity-after-earnings-39282/)  
  
\*\*14. Perion Network (PERI)\*\* — Q3 revenue was $90.8 million, down 18%  
from $110.5 million a year earlier, with the Affle deal still pending.  
The GAAP net loss widened to $9.9 million, or $0.29 a share, from a  
$4.1 million loss a year earlier.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/perion-network-peri-q3-2026-18-revenue-drop-amid-pending-affle-deal-39363/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/perion-network-peri-q3-2026-18-revenue-drop-amid-pending-affle-deal-39363/)  
  
Is the Datadog and Meta selloff just a guidance hangover, or are the  
AppLovin and Broadcom setups the more interesting ones right now?  
  
Not financial advice. Figures are from today's (Nov 16) write-ups,  
using intraday or latest-close prices, not live quotes. Price targets  
are targets, not promises.
